# What Stan cost us

## The integral solver would not hold

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```
Error in function tanh_sinh<double>::integrate:
The tanh_sinh quadrature evaluated your function
at a singular point and got -inf.

Warning: 243 chain(s) finished unexpectedly!
```

- 243 of 256 chains, dying after warmup, in the middle of sampling
- Nine days of tolerances, boundary fractions and midpoint
  approximations got that to 70 of 600
- `integrate_1d` errors rather than rejecting, and there is no
  `try`/`catch` to wrap it in
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```stan
// before
result = integrate_1d(
  primary_censored_integrand, lower_bound, d,
  theta, {d, pwindow}, ids, 1e-2
);

// after
result = ode_rk45(
  primary_censored_ode, y0, lower_bound, {d},
  theta, {d, pwindow}, ids
)[1, 1];
```

- Recast as an ODE, **0 of 600**
:::
::::

::: {.attribution}
epinowcast/primarycensored#34 and PR #64, commit `1c4e6f1`, September
2024. Also reported four to five times faster, from one run rather than
a benchmark.
:::

## No user types, so distributions became integers

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```r
dist_id <- pcd_stan_dist_id(family_name)

stanvars_functions[[1]]$scode <- gsub(
  "dist_id", dist_id,
  stanvars_functions[[1]]$scode,
  fixed = TRUE
)
```

::: {.attribution}
`epidist/R/marginal_model.R:339-368`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
- The type parameter is an integer, pushed into Stan source as text,
  from another language
- `dist_id = 3` meant Normal in Stan and Weibull in R. Asking for a
  Weibull fitted a normal and returned numbers
- Every distribution was affected except lognormal, gamma and
  exponential
- The fix was a 228 line test whose only job is checking that two
  integer tables agree
:::
::::

::: {.callout-important}
`primary_censored(Weibull(2, 1), Uniform(0, 1))` carries the type. There
is no second table for it to disagree with.
:::

## No imports, so we wrote a vendoring tool

- Stan has no package manager and no import statement, so a downstream
  model has to physically contain the text of the functions
- `R/pcd-stan-tools.R` is 453 lines. It lists the Stan functions,
  returns their source as an R string, and resolves the call graph in
  topological order
- The bundle it writes is checked in as `pcd_functions.stan`, 1081
  lines, and its first line is a comment reading
  `// Stan functions from primarycensored version 1.3.0.9000`
- A version number in a comment is the entire dependency story
- A hand-rolled parser, in R, over Stan source, to do what `using` does
